title: Now Thank We All Our God
description: Martin Rinkart's thanksgiving hymn in Catherine Winkworth's English, sung to Johann Crüger's tune Nun danket in the four parts The Hymnal of 1916 credits to Felix Mendelssohn, for 2 to 4 singers: verses 1 and 2, slow and broad.

credits.words: Martin Rinkart, "Nun danket alle Gott", translated by Catherine Winkworth (Lyra Germanica, second series, 1858)
credits.arrangement: Felix Mendelssohn's harmony as The Hymnal (1916) prints it, adapted by Stackapella

licence.words: public domain: Rinkart died 1649; Winkworth's translation was printed in Lyra Germanica, second series (London, 1858), and she died 1878
licence.tune: public domain: Crüger died 1662 (The Hymnal of 1916 dates the tune 1647); Zahn and Julian date it 1648
licence.arrangement: Felix Mendelssohn's four parts as The Hymnal (1916) prints them, "Harmonized by Felix Mendelssohn, 1809-1847" (public domain: Mendelssohn died 1847; printed 1916), adapted for 2 to 4 beginners: his tune unchanged; every part sung one note to a syllable, so where a part moves within a syllable, one of its notes is kept (the tune keeps its two slurred notes on "blessed" and "guide"); the alto and tenor revoiced in many chords so the alto takes the chord's third under the tune and the tenor a note the alto leaves (for example A4 and B-flat 4 under the C5s and D5s of lines 1 and 3, where he has F4; G4 under "heart", making a G minor six-four where he has D4; E4 under "world", "arms" and "still"; F-sharp 4 under "count-"; A3 under "ours" and "day", where he has C4; and the tenor on G3 under "from", where he has D4); in lines 2 and 4 the alto sings A3, a sixth under the tune, on the held F4 where he writes the alto in unison with it; the bass keeps his chords with fewer leaps: line 1 stays on F3 and B-flat 3 (he has A3 on "we" and B-flat 2 on "our"), "With heart, and" is F3, D3, C3 (he has F2, G2, A2, and F2 on the second "and"), "In Whom" is A2, B-flat 2, with the alto on his F4 and a G minor chord on "Whom" (he has F3 and E3, then D3 under B-flat), his rising F2, G2, A2, B2, C3 under "moth-er's arms" is sung F2, A2, C3, and "count-less" holds F-sharp 3, with a D7 on "less" (where he has E3 rising to F-sharp 3); "still" is C major for his G minor (alto E4, his own second note on "And"), to avoid a bare fourth under the tune; the bass on "still" is C3 (he has B-flat 2); "drous" stays on F3 (he has F3 and E-flat 3); "re-" in line 4 is A minor (his tenor's C-sharp in the second half left out); the two fermatas ("voi-ces," and "re-joi-ces;") held four beats, which adds a bar after each; the Amen left out; and breaths written in for beginners
licence.source: The Hymnal, as authorized and approved for use by the General Convention of the Protestant Episcopal Church in the United States of America in the year of our Lord MCMXVI (New York: The Church Pension Fund, 1916), Hymn 422, "Deo Gratias", p. 523, headed "Johann Crüger, 1647. Harmonized by Felix Mendelssohn, 1809-1847." and "May be sung in unison.", in F as printed and as written here, printed in minims (4/2) and written here in crotchets (4/4) with a one-crotchet pickup; verse 1 as printed under the notes and verse 2 as printed below them (the page prints two verses; the words credited there "Martin Rinkart, c. 1636; Tr. Catherine Winkworth, 1858" (Winkworth's own 1858 book signs them "Martin Rinckart. 1636."; Julian gives 1663)); the Amen left out; read from Princeton Theological Seminary Library's copy at archive.org/details/authoriz00epis (scan page n596). The tune checked note for note against The English Hymnal (London: Humphrey Milford, Oxford University Press, and A. R. Mowbray, an undated printing of the 1906 edition), Hymn 533, "Nun Danket", "Present form of melody by J. Crüger, 1598-1662", pp. 688 to 689, in F, which prints the same melody under an unsigned harmony, University of Toronto Faculty of Music Library's copy at archive.org/details/englishhymnalwit00unse (scan pages n722 and n723); the words checked against Winkworth's own Lyra Germanica, second series: The Christian Life (London: Longman, Brown, Green, Longmans and Roberts, 1858), pp. 145 to 146, "The Chorus of God's Thankful Children", archive.org/details/lyragermanicasec00bunsrich (scan pages n165 and n166), whose "bless'd" and "perplex'd" The Hymnal spells out. Breaths written in for beginners: "God,", "done,", "arms", "way", "love," and verse 1's "day." (and the same notes in verse 2) each give up three quarters of a beat; the held "voi-ces," and "re-joi-ces;" (verse 2's "near us!" and "cheer us;") sound four beats and rest one before the next line.
